title: Exclude claude_version from reading_inputs so version bumps keep
summary: Config::reading_inputs resets [parallel] and [landing] before hashing; it should also blank agents.claude_version so a harness pin bump leaves queued readings valid and drain does not stall. Audience: the operator running drain, and the verifier running cargo test.

defaults_applied.how: Add a unit test and require cargo test and clippy to pass.
Fix the hash input rather than re-accepting stale readings.
The criterion checks that equal inputs result when only the version differs.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Only agents.claude_version is excluded; other [agents] fields can change what the reader sees and stay in.
The hash is computed by blanking the field on a clone, matching how parallel and landing are handled.
Already-stored readings made under the old hash are not migrated; this applies from the next bump on.

acceptance_criteria.text: A unit test in config.rs shows two configs differing only in agents.claude_version yield equal reading_inputs(), while a change to another setting (e.g. budget.job_usd) still yields different output. Run: cargo test -p athena-data reading_inputs
cargo test and cargo clippy --all-targets pass across the workspace, and cargo fmt --check is clean.
The reading_inputs doc comment and the docs in run.rs/capability.rs and CHANGELOG state that the claude_version pin, like [parallel] and [landing], does not invalidate a reading, with the reason.
Other agents settings (env_pass, timeouts, host_baseline_tokens) still count toward reading_inputs; only the version pin is excluded.

out_of_scope: Changing the pinned version in athena.toml
Migrating stored readings or changing drain acceptance logic
departures: The change is small and well localised, so pass probability is above the reference.
